import pandas as pd

def load_and_prepare_source(filepath: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Load a source CSV file and ensure the schema and dtypes match the target schema.
    """
    # Define the target schema dtypes
    dtype_map = {
        'tripduration': 'int64',
        'starttime': 'string',
        'stoptime': 'string',
        'start station id': 'Int64',  # Use pandas nullable integer dtype
        'start station name': 'string',
        'start station latitude': 'float64',
        'start station longitude': 'float64',
        'end station id': 'Int64',
        'end station name': 'string',
        'end station latitude': 'float64',
        'end station longitude': 'float64',
        'bikeid': 'Int64',
        'usertype': 'string',
        'birth year': 'Int64',
        'gender': 'Int64'
    }

    # Read CSV with no dtype enforcement first (to avoid parsing errors)
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)

    # Ensure all expected columns exist
    expected_columns = list(dtype_map.keys())
    missing_cols = set(expected_columns) - set(df.columns)
    if missing_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing columns in source file {filepath}: {missing_cols}")

    # Select and reorder columns to target schema order
    df = df[expected_columns]

    # Convert dtypes carefully
    # For integer columns that may have missing values, use pandas nullable Int64 dtype
    for col, dtype in dtype_map.items():
        if dtype == 'Int64':
            # Convert to pandas nullable integer dtype
            df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
        elif dtype == 'int64':
            # For tripduration, convert to int64, fill NaNs with 0 or drop rows if any
            df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce')
            if df[col].isnull().any():
                # If tripduration has NaNs, drop those rows (tripduration is critical)
                df = df.dropna(subset=[col])
            df[col] = df[col].astype('int64')
        elif dtype == 'float64':
            df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce')
        elif dtype == 'string':
            df[col] = df[col].astype('string')
        else:
            # fallback: convert to string
            df[col] = df[col].astype('string')

    # After conversions, drop rows with critical missing values if any remain
    # Critical columns: tripduration, starttime, stoptime, start station id, end station id, bikeid
    critical_cols = ['tripduration', 'starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station id', 'end station id', 'bikeid']
    df = df.dropna(subset=critical_cols)

    # Reset index after dropping rows
    df = df.reset_index(drop=True)

    return df

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_2/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_2/test_1.csv"
    ]

    # Load and prepare each source file
    dfs = []
    for filepath in source_files:
        df = load_and_prepare_source(filepath)
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source dataframes into one target dataframe
    target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Final schema enforcement (optional, but ensures consistency)
    # Convert 'usertype' values to string and strip whitespace if any
    target_df['usertype'] = target_df['usertype'].str.strip()

    # Export the combined dataframe to the target CSV path
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_2/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
